# Suttatthasamuccayabhūmi (Pe 6)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Suttatthasamuccayabhūmi* ("The Sixth Stage: Compendium of Discourse Meaning") is the sixth chapter of the *Peṭakopadesa* [Giacomella Orofino and Silvio Vita 2004]. The text functions as an exegetical compendium providing scholastic analysis and definitions of core doctrinal concepts [Stuart 2012]. In treating terms such as the aggregates (*khandha*), it employs repetitive definitional formulas (e.g., Pe 6.60, defining *khandhattho* as *samūhattho*, *puñjattho*, and *rāsattho*) that find direct stylistic and scholastic parallels in contemporaneous literature from Northwest India, including an unpublished Gāndhārī *Saṅgītisūtra* commentary and the *Nettipakaraṇa* [Stuart 2012; Stuart, Yogācāra Substrata].

Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reveals extensive Pali-internal reuse across 169 texts (3,351 matches), showing its closest correspondences with the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Nettippakaraṇa* (*Padaṭṭhānahāravibhaṅga*), the *Sotāpatti Saṃyutta* (SN 55), the *Majjhimanikāya-aṭṭhakathā*, and various Abhidhamma and Nikāya collections [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese treatises, exhibiting substantial shared phrasing with the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and its commentary, Śāntideva's *Bodhicaryāvatārapañjikā*, Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha*, the Chinese *Yuanqi jing* (T 124), and Tibetan translations of the *Yogācārabhūmi* and the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* [DharmaNexus].
